The nbfx Property API defines the annotation with which a module contributes a JavaFX property editor for a value type.
The module contains the SOURCE-retention @PropertyEditorRegistration annotation and a LayerGeneratingProcessor that writes NbFx/PropertyEditors entries into the compiling module's generated layer. The property-sheet reader consumes those entries through LayerPaths.
A module declares a property editor with @PropertyEditorRegistration; the generated layer supplies its value type, position and inline-editing capability.
The processor is covered by a unit test that asserts the generated layer fragment for a sample annotated source. The module API is marked under development until the MVP freeze, after which API signature tests (sigtest) are enabled.
A JDK is required to compile the annotation processor.
Only com.gluonhq.netbeans.nbfx.api.property is public. The processor implementation is an implementation detail and is not exported.
The processor is discovered by the compiler through the META-INF/services/javax.annotation.processing.Processor service, generated by @ServiceProvider(service=Processor.class).
See lookup-lookup.
Yes. The processor creates NbFx/PropertyEditors/<value-type>.instance entries.

The annotation processor runs in the compiler's processing rounds and is stateless. It does not touch the JavaFX thread.
No code runs on startup; the module only contributes a compiled annotation processor.
